sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has threatened to ban all Eritreans from entering the UK if the east African country's government does not accept more returns of small boat migrants and foreign national offenders.

sentences.text: From Thursday, Eritrean diplomats will face restrictions on their movement outside London.
sentences.article_title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy

sentences.text: Fast-track visas will also be stopped for VIPs.
sentences.article_title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy

sentences.text: Ministers have previously pressured other countries into accepting returns by threatening visa bans.
sentences.article_title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy

sentences.text: Eritreans were the most common nationality among small boats migrants in the 12 months to June - accounting for 18% of arrivals , external , according to figures from the House of Commons Library.

sentences.text: The Eritrean embassy in London has been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy

sentences.text: "Eritrea has had every chance to accept the return of criminals and those with no right to be in the UK.

sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: On a rainy Wednesday afternoon, a novelty toy and games store in a quiet part of New York City was seeing much busier foot traffic than usual.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (£11,000).
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: "Y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she said, referring to a scene from the 1990 romantic comedy film where Roberts' character is treated poorly by staff at a  shop, who imply she cannot afford various items.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: In a follow-up post on social media, Clarkson said the store had told her the bird cost $15,000 and that they could find her something else "comparable".
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: Art of Play has defended how it treated the star on social media, saying the wooden bird - which is called Molly - is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: They also said they had offered her a different singing bird for $2,000 from a clock-making shop in Germany, which she could have purchased that day.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: "Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," Art of Play said.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: A shopkeeper said they would not comment on the story anymore and just wanted to get back to business as usual.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: Molly still hung on the wall at the shop, this time next to a price tag of $15m.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: The sign jokes that the sculpture is the "world's most famous singing bird automata!" The store's owner has said he and his staff have faced threats and harassment after Clarkson's complaint, telling the BBC's US partner CBS News that the singer had endangered them.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: This week, a man filmed himself yelling expletives outside the store, before accusing its employees of "racially profiling" Clarkson.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: Customer Emily Trantanella likes Art of Play The kerfuffle lingered in headlines on Wednesday as a news outlet released surveillance video from Art of Play purporting to show Clarkson's visit.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: The grainy footage, which has no audio, is said to show her wearing a yellow shirt, a baseball cap and a backpack while browsing items, including Molly the bird.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: She can be seen talking with an employee - apparently about the bird as she points at it - and later moving to leave the store.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: She comes back in to say something animatedly to the cashier.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: But while the argument over the bird has gone viral online, some of Art of Play's customers had not heard about it before being greeted by news cameras on the premises.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: One customer who was in town visiting his daughter said he was not familiar with the controversy.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: For others, Clarkson's claims that those at the store had treated her rudely came as a surprise.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.text: Kiran Ramineni, who lives next door, described Art of Play as a "very nice small mom and pop store" and said he had seen flocks of journalists there in recent days.
sentences.article_title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird

sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Do you really need protein powder to build muscle?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For teenage boys and girls "you can get all the protein that you need from food alone", says registered dietitian Nichola Ludlam-Raine.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Protein shakes, powders or bars can be useful for some, including high-level athletes and those who have certain allergies, but they should not replace a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: There can also be some unwanted side effects from using protein powders such as bloating, gas, cramps, and diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Those with pre-existing health conditions should not use it unless they have been told they can by their doctor.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Ludlam-Raine points out that the protein powder market is not as tightly regulated as medicines.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "Of course, you can get reputable companies who do third-party testing and make sure that what you see on the label is what is in the inside, but that's not always the case," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "And ultimately you can't just have a shake and your biceps grow." Some protein powders contain high amounts of added sugar, artificial ingredients, and hidden stimulants.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Dr Ramnik Mathur is a consultant paediatrician from Chelsea and Westminster NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: He explains that we need micronutrients like zinc, calcium and magnesium, which are found in whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, if meals are replaced with protein shakes, those nutrients are lost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Experts suggest spreading out protein across the day and aiming for 20-25g per meal.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you're keen to up your intake, try some of these recipes.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: During puberty when children have growth spurts, they do need more protein because their body is growing rapidly, building new muscle and bone mass.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Mathur says there are risks to eating too much protein.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "If you look at social media, they'll say you need to eat a lot of protein, but your body can handle only so much." He explains that if you eat too much, it has to be excreted by the kidneys and liver which can become overloaded.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If they still want to use it, speak to a registered dietitian or nutritionist first.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Now off I go to tell my son the answer is still no - and the experts say the same. £170 a bag?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Artefacts from the ship were found just off the coast of Kekova Island The world's oldest shipwreck has been discovered off the coast of Turkey, archaeologists say.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: They have dated it to between 4,400 and 4,700 years old, which is the Early Bronze Age, and is around the same time that the Great Pyramid was being built.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The ship's wooden structure has not survived, but the ceramic storage pots it was carrying were lying on the sea floor and, remarkably, some still contain traces of what they held inside.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The archaeologists who found the ship say it was about 10m in length and was a trade vessel carrying cargo across the Mediterranean Sea.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "The shipwreck is a time capsule at the bottom of the sea," said Prof Hakan Öniz, from Akdeniz University in Turkey, who led the Mediterranean Archaeology Association expedition.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The divers found three stone anchors, as ships carried spares on long voyages The wreck is close to the shore of Kekova Island in Antalya, Turkey.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The artefacts lie scattered across an underwater slope,  just 30m beneath the waves.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Three large stone anchors were found, as well as more than 30 ceramic storage pots, called amphorae.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The fact that none of the ship's wood remained meant techniques like radiocarbon dating - which measures a form of carbon in organic materials - could not be used to determine its age.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Instead, archaeologists analysed the shape of the amphorae.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Because pottery styles have changed over time, different styles are linked to particular periods.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The Kekova ceramics are distinctive, with two handles, a ridge in the middle and a flat base. Öniz said this design matched other amphorae unearthed in Egypt and the Middle East that were known to be 4,400-4,700 years old.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "Comparing the decoration techniques… we can definitely say our wreck is Early Bronze Age.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Dr Karin Sowada, an archaeologist from Macquarie University, Australia, examined the amphorae after they were recovered.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Some were intact and she was surprised to see they still contained a viscous, glossy residue.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "I looked inside and nearly fainted.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: I could not believe how much [residue] was visible.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: It wasn't just like spots…. a lot of this material was still remaining," she said.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The team is now working to find out exactly what was being carried in the amphorae.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "It could be olive oil, it could be wine, it could be tree resins," Sowada said.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "It's possible that [the residue] could actually be the result of reuse of the jars.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: I mean, these jars are huge - they're not things that you just ship away and then never see again.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: People would have emptied these jars on arrival and potentially used them for many, many, many years." The wreck and its cargo are also shedding light on trade in the ancient world.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The archaeologists say the ship started its voyage from somewhere along the eastern coast of the Mediterranean.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: They believe it was taking goods to either the ancient city of Troy, in what is now north-western Turkey, or to the Minoan people in Crete.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The divers worked underwater to carefully excavate the artefacts Travelling by sea was fraught with danger, particularly around Kekova Island, where the strong currents and winds have claimed many ships.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: There are hundreds of wrecks in the area, and the Mediterranean Archaeology Association specialises in finding and studying them. Öniz says that when he is diving on the wreck his first thoughts are about the lives of the people who were connected to this vessel.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "We are the first humans who [have] touched these objects after 5,000 years.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: "We are always thinking of the sailors... the producers of the amphora and the person who carried the amphora on their shoulders to the ship, and the women who were waiting for their husbands, and they unfortunately couldn't go back." The shipwreck is owned by the Turkish Ministry of Culture.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Its minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy said the artefacts that have been recovered would be put on display in the new Mediterranean Underwater Archaeology Museum in Antalya when it opens in the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: Previously, the record holder was a wreck off the coast of Dokos, an island in southern Greece, which dates to about 4,200 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Shipwreck thought to be 4,700 years old found off coast of Turkey

sentences.text: The oldest known intact shipwreck, where the wood is still preserved, was found in the Black Sea off the coast of Bulgaria.

sentences.article_title: 'I'd talk to the TV': The paid companions bringing warmth to China's lonely

sentences.text: Waiting times for driving tests have dropped below 20 weeks for the first time since November 2024, according to official figures.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: But learner drivers in September still had to wait an average of 19.7 weeks, or around five months, for a practical test.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) has been trying to cut waiting times and clear a backlog which began during the Covid pandemic in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Commenting on the agency's progress, one driving instructor told the BBC: "I don't think this is anything to boast about." The DVSA initially had hoped to reduce the average waiting time to seven weeks by the end of last year.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander pushed the target back to summer 2026, but subsequently admitted even that would not be possible - with waits not expected to fall to seven weeks until next autumn .
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: The DVSA conducted 191,682 practical driving tests in September, with more than half of those passing.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Learner drivers have repeatedly told the BBC how a lack of access to driving tests has limited their freedom, education and job prospects.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Until earlier this year, many learner drivers chose to pay inflated prices to access driving tests being resold by third party providers who'd used automated programmes, or bots, to block book tests before learners could access them.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: But a number of changes were made to the test booking system earlier this year by the DVSA to stop the system being exploited.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Now, only the learner driver is able to book their driving test.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: Justin Madders, the minister for roads, said the government "inherited record waiting times and a significant backlog".
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: "While driving test waiting times are still not where we want them to be, these figures show real progress is being made," he added.
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: A DVSA spokesperson said the agency was "committed to reducing waiting times" and that "examiner numbers are at their highest level since November 2017".
sentences.article_title: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks

sentences.text: "But we know there's more to do and we won't stop until every learner can get a test slot when they need one, wherever they're learning to drive," the spokesperson added.

sentences.text: About 400 postmen and women are leaving Royal Mail per week, according to the Communication Workers Union (CWU), who claims this number has gone up since the company introduced a new delivery system earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of Royal Mail staff quitting each week under new efficiency plans

sentences.text: The CWU says the firm had been losing about 330 postal staff a week from a workforce of 83,000 before it rolled out DM26, which reorganised routes to improve delivery performance.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of Royal Mail staff quitting each week under new efficiency plans

sentences.text: The union claims the new system is not working in hundreds of offices, and BBC Your Voice has heard from staff warning of a "nightmare" Christmas ahead as the number of parcels increases.

sentences.text: Royal Mail says the reforms are part of its plan to deliver a more "efficient and financially sustainable" service.

sentences.text: Over the last year we've been in touch with more than 30 postal staff in all four nations of the UK, as they have switched over to DM26.

sentences.text: It allows for second class post to only be delivered every other weekday, and is supposed to guarantee first class mail and parcels are delivered every day, by putting workers into groups of three and changing the walking pattern of rounds.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of Royal Mail staff quitting each week under new efficiency plans

sentences.text: But posties speaking to us anonymously say parcels are still being prioritised, letters left behind, and time wasted in sorting and dividing mail into first and second class.

sentences.text: Rules is an "outstanding example of living history", the National Trust said The home of London's oldest restaurant, which has hosted famous faces from Charles Dickens to Madonna over the past two centuries, has been given to the National Trust.

sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.text: He said staff put a lot of thought into where they sit certain people, such as rival film directors or opposing political politicians.

sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.text: "It has defied the odds to be standing here today, doors still open and treacle sponge still on the menu.
sentences.article_title: Home of oldest restaurant given to National Trust

sentences.text: A call comes in over the radio about a stolen Ford Transit van.
sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: Within 25 minutes officers have found it, chased it down and arrested a suspect.
sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: Despite a recent drop, vehicle thefts are up almost 50% in England and Wales compared with a decade ago, according to Home Office data.
sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: Last year, just 3% of vehicle theft offences resulted in a charge or summons.
sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: As well as spending time on the front line in London and Sussex, we have privately spoken to 20 police officers from six forces.
sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: They told us while they have the skills and experience to tackle vehicle crime, they are overstretched, under-resourced and struggling to keep pace with increasingly sophisticated criminal networks.

sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.article_title: One stolen every four minutes - inside the police battle against vehicle thieves

sentences.text: China is the world's largest toymaker, producing the majority of toys on sale in the US On the underside of most children's toys on sale in the US you'll find the same three words – "Made in China".
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: As retailers prepare their stocks for the festive rush, be they online giants or "mom-and-pop" physical stores, the BBC World Service's Follow the Money series traces how a toy gets from a factory in China to the US.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: And where the money goes.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Guangdong province, which neighbours Hong Kong in southern China, is the heart of the country's toy manufacturing industry.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: In the city of Dongguan workers on the floor of the Mihox factory pop plastic toys out of steel moulds, and pile them into crates ready for painting.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: The company says it employs more than 800 people and makes around 55 million toys a year for the American market, which represents half of its business.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Follow the money: The journey of a $30 toy from China to America Every toy starts with a design from a customer, such as an American toy company.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: The factory then makes a prototype, and builds moulds from which plastic parts and other components are formed.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Going from the first idea to finished toy takes one to two years, says Melanie Wang from the Mihox sales team.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Much of that is the customer going back to the drawing board.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: "They modified the design again, again, and again to improve it." Once the design is signed off, things move more quickly.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: A mould takes about a month to make, and the production run lasts about three months.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: The Mihox factory in Dongguan employs more than 800 people So, how much of the US retail price does the factory get?
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: On a $30 toy, that's $6, which has to cover the price of the plastic and other materials, production costs including wages, and what profit the factory makes.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Chinese factories typically make a profit of between 3% and 10%, according to Jay Foreman, chief executive of US toy firm Basic Fun.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: So for a $30 toy that's between 60 and 18 cents of the $6 the factory charges to make it.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Samson Ko is president of the Toys Manufacturers' Association of Hong Kong.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Many of his members moved their factories across the border into mainland China in the 1980s, attracted by cheaper land and labour.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: He says the way toys are made has barely changed since then.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: "Automation now takes place mostly in the moulding and the packaging process.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: But for soft toys, or even some of the electronics nowadays, it's still very labour intensive." And Chinese labour isn't cheap anymore, he adds, after recent rises.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Melanie Wang explains that Mihox gets 20% of a toy's retail price Average pay in Vietnam is about half of that in China, said one report , external at the start of this year.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Yet fewer than 10% of Ko's members have moved any production outside China, and in those cases mostly only because customers asked them to do so.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: The Chinese factories remain busy, he says, because a single toy can undergo more than one manufacturing process, from moulding the parts, to adding electronics, sewing materials, and final assembly.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: This often requires it travelling to different factories.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Ko adds that in Guangdong these separate facilities are located close to each other, and used to "working in harmony".
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: He says this makes the whole manufacturing process run more smoothly than in other countries.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: From the factory, the toy goes by truck to a port, such as Shenzhen, the biggest in Guangdong.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Ivy Tse is co-founder of FreightAmigo, a Hong Kong logistics company that runs an online platform for both Hong Kong and mainland China exporters.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: These businesses can book a cargo container, sea passage to an overseas destination, arrange insurance cover, and secure finance.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Tse says it takes about 15 days for a cargo ship to get from Shenzhen to the US west coast, and 25 to 30 days to the east coast.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: This year's Christmas toys left China in August and September.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Freight, from factory to the US, usually adds about 10% to the manufacturing cost of a toy, adds Tse.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: So if we stick to a toy that retails for $30 in the US, and therefore costs $6 to make in China, the cost of getting it to the states is 60 cents.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Once the toy reaches the US there is currently a tariff on Chinese toys that has to be paid to the US Customs and Border Protection (CBP).
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Following talks between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last month, the two governments have recommended toys for lower tariffs.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: But no new rate or start date has been set, and the US must first hold a public consultation.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: For now the basic rate is 12.5%, and some toys pay more.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: This is charged on the manufacturing price of the toy, not on how much it retails for.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: So for a $30 toy, that basic rate is 12.5% of $6, which is 75 cents.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: This tariff is paid for by the American company that has imported the toys.

sentences.text: One such firm is Learning Resources, a family business based near Chicago that sells educational toys.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Half of these it imports from China.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: "We pay 100% of the tariffs, let there be no doubt about that," says the company's chief executive Rick Woldenberg.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Jay Foreman says that most of the money spent on a toy in the US doesn't leave the country The cost of making the $30 toy, getting it to the US, and paying the import tariff, comes to $7.35.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: So that leaves $22.65, or 75.5% of the total.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: That money never leaves the US, explains Foreman from Basic Fun.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: His firm, which is based in Florida, makes Tonka trucks and Care Bears cuddly toys.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: "It's kept by my company, the [US] transportation company, the retailer," he says.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: If we allow $2.65 for the US delivery firm, the toy company and the retailer will typically share the remaining revenues 50-50.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: So that would give them $10 each.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: While profit margins are commercially sensitive and therefore not generally revealed, industry studies show that the toy firm and retailer would usually make a profit of up to 25% or $2.50.
sentences.article_title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer

sentences.text: Getting a toy onto the shelves in the US requires both a lot of work and a long journey.

sentences.text: Wayfair is among three firms which have been fined £6m in total by the competition watchdog for illegally using misleading sales tactics – with some customers set to receive refunds.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: The online furniture retailer was fined £4.8m for misleading customers with time-limited offers, while online electronics seller Appliances Direct was fined £1.2m for the same practice, the Competition Markets Authority (CMA) said.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Gold's Gym has been fined £45,000 for not telling customers the total price of its memberships.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: It and Appliances Direct have been ordered to refund customers a total of £440,000.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Wayfair and Appliances Direct said the CMA's fines were disproportionate.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Gold's Gym has been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Thousands of Appliances Direct customers will receive refunds of £25 each on average while 726 Gold's Gym customers will get refunds of up to £50, according to the CMA.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: The watchdog said customers do not need to take any action and both companies will contact those affected customers about refunds.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Appliances Direct has been told to pay refunds by 11 March, while Gold's Gym has been given a deadline of 29 March.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: The CMA said Wayfair, Appliances Direct, and Gold's Gym had "engaged constructively" with its investigation.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: They all admitted to breaking the law and agreed to settle the case early, it added.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: The watchdog said their co-operation reduced the firms' fines by 40%.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Eight firms under investigation over online pricing AA and BSM ordered to refund learner drivers for hidden fees A Wayfair spokeswoman said the penalty was "excessive" but that "we take the CMA's findings seriously and we chose to settle so we can continue to focus on serving our customers".

sentences.text: Nick Glynne, chief executive of Buy it Direct, which owns Appliances Direct and several other online retailers, accepted that its practices were wrong, but said the firm should have simply been given "a rap on the knuckles" instead.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: Hayley Fletcher, senior director for consumer protection at the CMA, said: "At a time when many households are carefully managing their budgets, people shouldn't lose out because of misleading sales tactics.

sentences.text: "Businesses must treat their customers fairly and make sure they comply with the law - or risk hefty fines." Sue Davies, head of consumer rights policy at Which?, praised the CMA's response.
sentences.article_title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for misleading sales tactics

sentences.text: "The refunds secured by the CMA are a much-needed win for consumers at a time when household budgets are under strain," she said.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Could using AI in your job application be ruining your chances of getting hired?

sentences.text: Tom, 22, from Maidstone graduated last year with a geography degree and says he applied for over 200 jobs before finally landing a role last month as a restaurant manager.

sentences.text: He says the process was "exhausting" and "demoralising", with employers often not even getting back to him, and he wouldn't have got through it without some help from AI.

sentences.text: "That's where it feels like a weird tightrope.

This summer, the Institute of Student Employers (ISE) surveyed 155 of the UK's biggest graduate employers and found they were becoming "more accepting" of candidates using AI "at some stages of the recruitment process".
sentences.article_title: 'I applied for 200 jobs' - How 'spray and pray' AI job applications can backfire

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding technology may be a drop in the bucket, as it doesn't create rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For example, Rainmaker's 19 million gallons equates to around 0.01 inch of rain across 100 square miles.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Nevertheless, more than 50 countries , external are developing programmes to modify the weather and a surge of start-ups are developing systems to create rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: As well developed and promising as this innovative field has become, these businesses continue to face thorny questions on safety and efficacy, leading to novel approaches with both finding the right material to spray into clouds and how they do it.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Augustus Doricko with a Rainmaker drone Augustus Doricko, the founder and CEO of Rainmaker, is quick to answer any questions on the consequences of how his company uses the silver iodide compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: It's clear he's been asked about chemical safety many times.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He says Rainmaker releases this form of silver at 20 grams per flight, distributed across thousands of square kilometres.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding sessions have to wait for clouds to form to try to coax them into precipitation.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Their drones are outfitted with silver iodide flares, and when lit the burning atomizes the water particles into a small enough size so they can stay suspended in the freezing cloud for hours, eventually turning into crystals and later rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Rainmaker operates in states such as Idaho, Utah, Colorado and areas of the Middle East such as Jordan.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: A year later, silver iodide was found to be more effective than dry ice, which quickly turns into useless gas.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While seeding agents caused more rainfall, they didn't move the needle much.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In fact, sobering statistics point to how patchy this technology can be in what it pours on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "With the right conditions, cloud seeding squeeze out about an extra five to 10% of precipitation," says Jon Meyer, an assistant state climatologist with the Utah Climate Center.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: What was encouraging, though, for the cloud-seeding sector was a landmark 2017 study that found how silver iodide worked as expected, one of the first reports to observe cloud seeding in action using radar and precipitation gauges.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In the past several years, Meyer has been encouraged to see more companies such as Rainmaker bring innovation to an old industry.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "Drones [such as Rainmaker's products] present this new avenue," says Meyer, "and they offer a more targeted nature to these clouds we hope will be responsive." Olivia Li is developing an alternative to silver iodide for cloud seeding What is sprayed into clouds may also be undergoing a major shift.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Recast Systems in San Francisco is experimenting with a type of protein made from amino acids found in the soil, says CEO Olivia Li.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While still undergoing tests at Texas A&M University, this new seeding agent moves Recast away from silver iodide as the go-to compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It's safe, biodegradable and nucleates ice at a higher efficiency than silver iodide," says Li, whose company currently uses silver iodide to seed clouds in several US states.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Meyer is optimistic this technology's trajectory will only continue to rise.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "We're going to see more demand for these services as so many regions are experiencing water demand," he says, "and they're going to be looking for ways to help bridge that gap." X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Farmer Steve Cargil is now paid $200,000 a year for hosting a solar farm on his land Steve Cargil's family has farmed the flat, dry land around Uvalde, a small city in southwest Texas, since 1953.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil, 67, had always assumed that one of his three children would eventually take it over, the way he had from his father.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: But that assumption took a hit one night in 2018 after a violent hailstorm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil and his son, Ryan, had spent months nursing crops of cabbage and onions to harvest.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then a storm rolled through and destroyed them overnight.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "I remember my son saying, 'Dad, I just don't know if I can do this.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: You do everything right, and we work so hard, and you come out one morning and it's all gone'," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil's farm was at risk of ending with him, he says, with none of his three children wanting to farm full time.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: For years, that left him wondering what would happen to the land, and to his own retirement, since farmers rarely have a pension to fall back on.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then in 2001 Cargil signed a deal to lease 600 acres of his land, about a quarter of the total, to a company called OCI Energy which built a vast solar farm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "Never in my wildest dreams did I think that a solar project would be on my farm," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Looking back now, he calls it a blessing.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: The lease, which pays Cargil $200,000 (£150,000) a year, has let him keep his farm running through a punishing drought.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He has been able to concentrate his water irrigation allowance on the land he still farms, and he has stopped losing sleep over rises in the price of things such as diesel and fertiliser.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar farms can stretch out across the flat lands of Texas On hot afternoons, when demand for power peaks, solar is now regularly supplying around a third of the electricity used across Texas, says Mark Stover, executive director of the Texas Solar and Storage Association.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He says that the solar boom is being driven by two main things.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Firstly, it is cheap and quick to connect solar farms to Texas' power grid, which is separate to the rest of the US.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Secondly, Texas has a huge and growing appetite for electricity, driven by a burgeoning population.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, Texas's population increased by 15.8%, , external making it one of the fastest-growing states in the nation.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We need a whole lot of power in Texas, and we need it quickly," Stover says.

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
