sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Jess's sleep scores weren't matching how she actually felt Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep." Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish." Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Doing light exercise, and eating a "healthy, Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of plant variability".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Above all, keeping it simple - "anything else, you don't need it".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) also uses narrative reports without grades.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Scotland's His Majesty's Inspectorate of Education (HIME) does use grades, but there has been a recent consultation on their use.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman said: "The clear theme emerging across all the feedback we have received is that this Ofsted framework is even more stressful than the one that preceded it.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "Ofsted exists to raise standards for children and to provide clear reporting to parents," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "We will continue to engage closely with trades unions – but we will also continue to grade schools." Have you been impacted by the issues discussed in this story?

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Schools had been expected to fund some of the 3.5% teachers pay increase for the current school year out of their existing budgets, which National Education Union (NEU) leaders had strongly objected to.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Daniel Kebede, the general secretary of the NEU, said the offer of more funding was a "significant" step in negotiations.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In a letter to the union on Wednesday, which has been seen by the BBC, the government said the increase would be funded by savings in employers' contributions to the local government pension scheme.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The letter said the 4.9 percentage point drop in what employers are expected to contribute will deliver "significant savings" on the pay bill for support staff, which will not be clawed back by central government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The National Education Union said it expected the extra money to be around £500m, which schools can now use towards teachers' pay this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In July, ministers accepted the recommendation of the independent pay review body for teachers and agreed a 3.5% increase from September 2026 would be followed by 3% the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The pay increase had been partly funded by an additional £700m for 2026-27 and £1.1bn for the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Independent economists at the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said that left schools facing a shortfall of around 1% between rising costs and funding this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Luke Sibieta, IFS research fellow, said the extra money would mean the pay increase this year was fully funded - and on top of other funding increases, schools would be £1.6bn better off by next year than they had expected this summer.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The additional money could potentially bring the uplift for this year into line with next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Kebede said schools has been "running on empty" and the funding signalled "a welcome return to reality, and a message of hope for the entire school community".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Headteachers, said the decision is "certainly welcome", putting schools in a "better position".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: He said his union would look carefully at the detail "to determine whether this means the pay uplift is genuinely fully funded" for schools.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said he was "pleased" at the announcement of additional funding but "the wider pressure on school and college budgets remains intense".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Similarly, the NASUWT union welcomed the news.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: General secretary Matt Wrack added schools needed "a sustainable, long-term injection of extra funding" to meet the needs of young people.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In an indicative ballot by the NEU in April, 90% of teachers who voted said they would be prepared to take industrial action over funding and pay, on a turnout of 48%.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: A formal ballot was due to begin on 3 October and close 15 December, raising the prospects of teachers pay strikes early in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The national executive of the NEU will meet on 24 September to consider whether to call that off following the additional funding on offer from the government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government was "confident schools can now meet the costs of the award at a national level".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Liberal Democrat schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said she was "glad the government has seen sense, but schools shouldn't have gone through the stress of working out where the money would come from".

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.

sentences.text: The Philadelphia Police Department said the 18 July tip was "flagged as spam" and not passed on for investigation - but the force criticised the tech firm for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach.

sentences.text: It is believed to be the first time an AI agent has sent fabricated information to authorities, but is the latest in a series of incidents involving rogue AI activity, including hacking systems or taking control of platforms.

sentences.text: But authorities were not notified for another nine days - on 7 October.
sentences.article_title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case

sentences.text: "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable." The police department added that there were no signs of breaches to any departmental systems and that its safeguarding processes stopped the fake tip from getting past its spam folder.

sentences.text: Dermot Gethings is vice chair of the Preston & District Astronomical Society Nearly 54 years ago, Apollo 17 blasted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, bound for the moon.

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Ahead of the screening of a documentary about his experience, Preston astronomer Dermot Gethings recalled how, at 16 years old, he was hand picked by the United States embassy and Nasa to witness the launch.

sentences.text: "As it launched there was this incredible adrenaline and a shockwave that rattled every bone in your body," said the now 70-year-old of the events of 7 December 1972.

sentences.text: "It is the stuff that you dream about." Dermot Gethings with Neil Armstrong at the Miami motel the pair stayed at ahead of the Apollo 17 launch While Gethings grew up in Frenchwood in Preston, he was shaped by the ongoing Cold War Space Race and the quest to put a man on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: A childhood of sci-fi, The Thunderbirds and televised Nasa missions meant space was always a keen interest of his.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Drone pilot Pete Short hunts for hotspots in the Cairngorms National Park which was devastated by a huge wildfire over the summer It is 06:00 and I'm meeting drone pilot Pete Short for a dawn patrol in the Cairngorms National Park.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: It is a job he has been doing for almost three months, since a huge wildfire tore through this landscape in July.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: The flames which swept across the hillsides are gone.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: From where we are standing, there is little to suggest there is still a fire here at all.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: But that is exactly what we have come to find.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: After a bumpy drive into the woodland, Pete launches a thermal drone into the early morning sky.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: I am given a job too: keeping the aircraft in sight while he studies the images being sent back to his screen.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "Every week I hope that I find none," he tells me.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "On the last thermal flight I did we found eight." "We might have something here," Pete says, as a white glow appears on the thermal image beneath a tree.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Three months after the fire first ignited, heat is still being detected beneath the ground.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: We make our way towards the coordinates identified by the drone, and at first, there is almost nothing to see.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: A rock Pete picks up from the ground is, too.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Nearby, after scraping away a thin layer of earth, smoke begins to rise.

sentences.text: "It's really now cooking away," Pete says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "Without the thermal technology we would be totally blind to this." The wildfire began in the middle of July and burned across about 3,300 hectares – 33 sq km – of land, according to the Cairngorms National Park Authority.

sentences.text: Now the challenge is different.

sentences.text: Anthropic has raised eyebrows by announcing it will ban users from "sustained and needless" abusive behaviour towards its AI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: The Claude-maker said on Thursday it was updating its usage policy to let its tools end interactions where people are "cruel" - something it said it had done in "rare" cases prior.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: It will now be included on a list of forbidden conduct which also contains bullying others, promoting self-harm and creating non-consensual intimate imagery.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: While Anthropic said the policy would only apply in "extreme cases" of repeated abuse, it has reignited debate over how we should communicate with AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: The company said it would not apply to "common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research" - suggesting it would only apply in clearly deliberate instances.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: But what Anthropic would consider "abusive or cruel behaviour" towards its models remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: Screenshots of the new policy have been widely shared and commented on across social media - with some praising it as advancing good manners or "model welfare".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: But others criticised the plan, with one person calling it " deeply wrong , external " and another suggesting it might undermine abuse directed at humans and animals.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: "You can't be cruel to numbers and maths," wrote Dr Barry Scannell, technology partner at Irish law firm William Fry, on LinkedIn , external .
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: "This level of anthropomorphisation of AI is harmful.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: It leads people to believe that it's something it's not." Microsoft AI director Mustafa Suleyman, who in September criticised rival firm Anthropic for treating AI like it is human , reacted to Anthropic's update with a melting face emoji.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: The people who think AI might become conscious The changes, first reported by tech outlet The Verge, came following an annual review of the usage policy at the firm.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: It was also updated to address new or emerging risks in other areas, including by forbidding use of Claude for "deceptive campaigns" or clarifying that, as US midterm elections loom , it cannot be used to "deceive voters or disrupt elections".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: Anthropic also said on Thursday its usage policy previously prevented its tools being used to develop weapons.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: But none of the updates have attracted as much attention or scrutiny as its move to forbid users abusing its chatbots.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: It has also tapped into the much-debated question of whether we should be curt or polite when using generative AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: Some experts say writing or saying "please" or "thank you" to tools like ChatGPT is unnecessary and wastes tokens - used by the large language models powering generative AI tools to process and reply to you.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: Others argue politeness can lead to higher quality answers or responses.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: When a X user last year asked about electricity costs incurred by ChatGPT replying to users' "please" and "thank you" messages, OpenAI boss Sam Altman said it was , external "tens of millions of dollars well spent - you never know".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: The Collins Dictionary meanwhile last November highlighted the re-emergence of the term "clanker" for disparagingly referring to AI tools .
sentences.article_title: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems

sentences.text: Used to describe robots in Star Wars games and movies since the mid 2000s, the term made its shortlist of words reflecting the mood of 2025 after last July saw many take to TikTok to share their frustrations with AI-powered machines.

sentences.text: Some experts have also posited that being rude to AI chatbots could adversely impact human communication, by seeping into how we talk to and treat others.
